findings.finding: exec_real on Windows spawns the real program as a grandchild of the launcher. The plan does not verify that this grandchild dies when the stub is killed. As far as I can tell from distlib's launcher source, its job object sets SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK as well as KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. If so, the body's own children are not in the job and survive the kill, holding the inherited stdout/stderr pipes, so subprocess.run's post-timeout communicate() blocks. The planned timeout test only covers a body that sleeps directly, not an exec_real child.
findings.location: Approach (exec_real prelude: 'a child plus sys.exit on Windows'; 'kill-on-close job'); Testing (timeout=2 case)
scenarios: A watchdog test whose stub calls exec_real for a real, slow git operation hangs on Windows after the timeout fires.

findings.finding: exec_real's Windows arm ('a child plus sys.exit') is not shown to die with the stub, and its real-binary resolution is unspecified. distlib's launcher creates its job with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK, so processes the Python body spawns (the real git started by exec_real) are not placed in the kill-on-close job. They can outlive a TerminateProcess of the launcher and hold the inherited stdout/stderr pipes. The timeout test only covers a body that sleeps itself, not one blocked inside exec_real. Separately, the plan does not say how exec_real locates the real binary while excluding bin_dir. Resolving the bare name via PATH would find the stub itself (on Windows, its own git.exe) and recurse.
findings.location: Approach — 'A prelude defines `exec_real(argv)` ... a child plus `sys.exit` on Windows. The launcher runs the body inside a kill-on-close job'; Testing — timeout=2 kill case
scenarios: Windows: a watchdog test's stub delegates to a slow real git via exec_real. The watchdog kills the launcher, but the real git broke away from the job and keeps the pipe open, so communicate() blocks past the timeout and the test hangs.
Any OS: exec_real(['git', ...]) resolves 'git' through PATH and re-invokes the stub, causing unbounded recursion or a hang.

evidence: tests/unit/test_snapshot_git_watchdog_d33f.py:23 `_BOUND_S = 1` and :60 `monkeypatch.setattr(git_fetch, "_GIT_TIMEOUT", _BOUND_S)`. Every git call through the PATH wrapper, not only the slow subcommand, runs under this bound.
Previously the wrapper was `#!/bin/sh` with `exec "{real_git}"`, which adds almost no startup time
Plan Testing: 'a `timeout=2` kill raises TimeoutExpired well before the body's 60 s sleep' (this checks only the kill direction)
findings.finding: On Windows, every git call that reaches the stub, including pass-through calls, now goes through the distlib launcher, then usually a venv `python.exe` redirector, then interpreter startup, and only then `exec_real` starting the real git. The watchdog tests shrink the bound to 1 second (`_BOUND_S = 1` in test_snapshot_git_watchdog_d33f.py), and the pass-through calls are bound by it too. A freshly written unsigned `.exe` in tmp_path may also be scanned by Defender on its first launch. Under xdist load on a Windows runner, a pass-through call could exceed 1 s and be reported as a timeout on the wrong subcommand, so these tests could become flaky. The plan only checks timing in one direction: that a timeout=2 kill fires before a 60 s sleep. It never checks that pass-through calls finish well inside the bounds the ported tests use.
findings.location: Testing — tests/test_exe_stub.py bullet; port of test_snapshot_git_watchdog_d33f.py / test_snapshot_submodules_watchdog_c605.py
scenarios: On a loaded Windows xdist worker, the `rev-parse` pass-through before the slow `remote` call takes over 1 s, and test_resolve_ref_fails_closed_when_git_remote_times_out fails for the wrong reason or passes vacuously

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm, and pin with a test, whether the real child started by `exec_real` on Windows dies when the stub is killed; if the launcher's job lets children escape, have the Windows `exec_real` put its child in a kill-on-close job of its own (or otherwise ensure it dies with the body).
evidence: Plan: 'os.execv on POSIX (the watchdog kill lands on the real process, as the sh stubs' exec did), a child plus sys.exit on Windows'
tests/_isolation.py:35-41 uses `subprocess.run(..., timeout=5)`. On Windows, `run()` calls `communicate()` after `kill()` on timeout
Plan Testing checks the kill only against the body's own 60 s sleep, not a running exec_real child
findings.finding: The plan argues that 'the launcher runs the body inside a kill-on-close job, so killing the stub kills the body'. That covers the Python body only. On Windows, `exec_real` starts the real binary as a child of the body. The distlib/simple_launcher job is, as far as I recall, configured with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK, which means the body's own children are not placed in the job. If the watchdog kills the stub while a pass-through real git is running, that git may outlive the kill. After `kill()`, `subprocess.run` on Windows calls `communicate()` with no timeout, so it would wait on the pipes git still holds. The plan's POSIX `os.execv` equivalence ('the watchdog kill lands on the real process') has no Windows counterpart, and no test covers this case.
findings.location: Approach — 'A prelude defines exec_real(argv): ... a child plus sys.exit on Windows. The launcher runs the body inside a kill-on-close job'
scenarios: A probe times out while the stub is passing through to a slow real git, and the probe blocks on pipes held by the escaped git

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make Windows `exec_real` keep the real child inside the kill scope (e.g. its own KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job, or CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB avoided plus an explicit job), and add a test_exe_stub case where the stub hangs in the exec_real child (not the body) and the kill still reaps it.
evidence: Plan: 'os.execv on POSIX (the watchdog kill lands on the real process, as the sh stubs' exec did), a child plus sys.exit on Windows. The launcher runs the body inside a kill-on-close job, so killing the stub kills the body.'
src/rebar/_proc.py:32-41: on non-POSIX, reap_process_group only does proc.kill() then proc.wait(); it does no tree kill.
Partially-verified: from the simple_launcher source (from memory; not observed in this environment), the job LimitFlags include JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK as well as KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.

Planned test_exe_stub timeout case: 'a timeout=2 kill raises TimeoutExpired well before the body's 60 s sleep'. That covers only a body that sleeps itself, not a body blocked inside exec_real's child.
findings.finding: The plan says the Windows `exec_real` (spawn a child, then `sys.exit`) behaves like POSIX `os.execv`, so the watchdog kill lands on the real process. That likely doesn't hold. The distlib/simple_launcher job is created with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK. SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK lets any process in the job create children outside the job, so the real git that the body spawns breaks away. When the watchdog kills the launcher (reap_process_group on Windows only calls proc.kill() + wait()), the body dies but the real git keeps running, holding the pipes and locking files under tmp_path.
findings.location: Approach — `exec_real(argv)` prelude / 'The launcher runs the body inside a kill-on-close job, so killing the stub kills the body'
scenarios: A ported stub delegates to real git via exec_real, and that real git is the slow or blocked step. On Windows the timeout kills only the launcher and body; the git.exe grandchild survives, keeps pipe handles open, and blocks tmp_path cleanup with locked files.
subprocess.run(timeout=…) on Windows calls communicate() after kill(). If the orphan inherited the pipes, the test hangs instead of raising promptly.

If that holds, stubs installed by building an env dict (rather than mutating os.environ, e.g. monkeypatch.setenv) will not shadow git.exe on Windows. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how stubs reach PATH (os.environ via monkeypatch versus env=). Add a Windows case to tests/test_exe_stub.py that spawns bare `git` with PATH supplied only via `env=`, or document that ported tests must set os.environ PATH.
evidence: "`subprocess` on Windows calls CreateProcess, which resolves a bare `git` on `PATH` by appending `.exe` only"
"a bare-name `git` spawn runs the stub"
Platform fact: CPython bpo-8557, Windows Popen uses the calling process's PATH for executable search when env= is supplied.
findings.finding: On Windows, subprocess/CreateProcess resolves a bare program name against the PARENT process's PATH, not against the PATH in an `env=` mapping passed to Popen (CPython bpo-8557). The plan's stub-lookup design and its helper test ('a bare-name `git` spawn runs the stub') do not say how the stub's bin_dir reaches PATH. A stub bin dir supplied only via `env={...,'PATH':...}` — for example, rebar code or a test that builds a child env — would not shadow git.exe on Windows, though it works on POSIX.
findings.location: Approach — install_exe_stub / Testing — 'a bare-name `git` spawn runs the stub'
scenarios: Windows platform: a ported test passes the stub dir through an env= dict. CreateProcess finds the real C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe, the stubbed hang never happens, and the test fails with DID NOT RAISE, exactly the original symptom.

Plan: 'a real `<name>.exe` on Windows'; it does not say what the helper returns
findings.finding: The plan never says what `install_exe_stub(bin_dir, name, body)` returns. On Windows it writes `<name>.exe`, not `<name>`. Some ported tests don't look the stub up on PATH; they pass its literal path. `test_mutation_sandbox.py` monkeypatches `sb.shutil.which` to return `str(tmp_path / "sandbox-exec")`, which won't exist on Windows. Unless the helper returns the actual written path and the ported tests use it, `_seatbelt_works()` would try to run a file that doesn't exist, hit `OSError`, return False, and fail the 'accepts' test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that install_exe_stub writes its source with a generic `#!python` first line (matching distlib FIRST_LINE_RE), sets `ScriptMaker.executable = sys.executable` and `source_dir`, and lets ScriptMaker generate the real shebang.
evidence: Plan: 'It is packaged with distlib's ScriptMaker (... :346 _copy_script ...) ... a #!<sys.executable> script on POSIX, a real <name>.exe on Windows'
Existing stubs write `f"#!{sys.executable}\n"` (tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:51, :98).

Partially-verified: distlib `_copy_script` sets adjust=True only on a FIRST_LINE_RE match; otherwise it calls copy_file (from distlib source knowledge; installed file not readable through the repo-confined tool).
findings.finding: The plan doesn't say what source file the helper hands to ScriptMaker. `_copy_script` adds the launcher/.exe path only when the script's first line matches distlib's FIRST_LINE_RE (`^#!.*pythonw?[0-9.]*([ \t].*)?$`). Any other file is copied verbatim. A first line like `#!C:\...\python.exe` ends in `.exe` and doesn't match, so if the helper writes `#!{sys.executable}` (as the current stubs do), the Windows output would be a plain extensionless `git` with no launcher.
findings.location: Approach — `tests/_exe_stub.py::install_exe_stub` (ScriptMaker `_copy_script`, scripts.py:346)
scenarios: The helper writes the body with `#!{sys.executable}` on the Windows runner. ScriptMaker copies it unchanged, CreateProcess still resolves the real git.exe, and every ported test fails just as it did before the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: In install_exe_stub, write `'#!python\n' + prelude + body` to a temp source file. Build `ScriptMaker(source_dir, str(bin_dir), add_launchers=True)` with `maker.executable = sys.executable`, then call `maker.make(name)`. Assert the returned filename is `<name>.exe` on Windows.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Document in tests/_exe_stub.py, and apply in test_exe_stub, that on Windows the stub dir must be on the parent's os.environ PATH (monkeypatch.setenv) or reached by a child Python process; `env=` alone does not affect argv[0] lookup.
evidence: Python subprocess docs (Windows): when resolving the executable with shell=False, cwd does not override the current directory and env cannot override PATH. Partially-verified from documentation knowledge.

The existing ported targets use monkeypatch.setenv for PATH (d33f:59, c605:80, c2ba:105, b0e0:73, scc_loc:228). repo_isolation_guard:74/120 and metrics_polyglot_support:166 pass PATH via env= to a Python child, which resolves git from its own environment, so those work.
The plan doesn't say how test_exe_stub injects the stub dir.
findings.finding: The root-cause section explains Windows lookup as 'CreateProcess resolves a bare git on PATH by appending .exe'. It leaves out that Python's subprocess on Windows resolves argv[0] against the PARENT process's PATH: `env=` cannot override it, and CreateProcess searches the application directory, cwd and System32 before PATH. The new test_exe_stub case 'a bare-name git spawn runs the stub' and any newly ported direct spawn will work only if the stub dir is prepended to os.environ (monkeypatch.setenv), not passed only through `env=`.
findings.location: Root cause §1 / Testing — test_exe_stub 'a bare-name git spawn runs the stub'
scenarios: test_exe_stub calls subprocess.run(['git', ...], env={**os.environ, 'PATH': stub_dir + ...}). It passes on POSIX, but on Windows it runs the real git.exe, and the 'runs the stub' assertion fails or is accidentally skipped.
